newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end mixed, moribund trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end mixed, moribund trade.

text.p: Shares at Bombay exchange closed on Monday with little change in a day of dull activity as major operators stayed on the sidelines waiting to see whether former finance minister P. Chidambaram will rejoin the government.
The Bombay 30-share index ended 0,02 points higher at a provisional 3,825.59, off 3,850.57, the day's high.
"It was generally a lacklustre day," said Tushar Sarda, chief executive and president at Daewoo Securities.
"I guess people are still waiting to see if Chidambaram comes back," Sarda said.
G.K. Moopanar,leader of Chidambaram's regional Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC)party, will decide within two days if the TMC will rejoin the government. A decision was earlier due on Sunday.

The TMC, part of the centre-left United Front coalition, decided on April 19 to stay out of the government after the alliance chose Inder Kumar Gujral instead of Moopanar as its leader and next prime minister.
"Activity is shifting to some second-tier stocks which are attracting investment buying," said Govind Agarwal,institutional sales dealer at brokerage Motilal Oswal Securities.
Buying interest by investors was seen in specific stocks that included Digital Equipment, Infosys Technologies and Hero Hondo, Agarwal said.

"In general, the investment environment in India is improving day by day...," Mark Mobius, director - Templeton Asset Management (India) Pvt Ltd said in a letter to investors in the Templeton India Income Fund.
"We must now wait and watch for political developments which will determine if India is going to continue on a more rapid growth toward economic liberalisation and internationalisation."
"We tend to be optimistic," the global fund manager said.
The communist-led Left Front plans to seek a revision of income tax rate reductions proposed in the budget for 1997/98 (April-March) dampened market sentiment, dealers said.
Parliament will begin a long-delayed debate on the budget on Wednesday.
